answer: Seat caps graded by stake resist sybils. One attestation seat is cheap, but each extra seat needs a bond several times larger while its reward shrinks. An attacker filling the economy with identities therefore walks into a gale: costs climb steeply, income barely moves, and returns go negative before real influence is reached. Operators must declare shared control, so undeclared duplicates are pruned like weak shoots cut from a trellis. Without that rule a thousand addresses could cast one hollow vote and pass as a crowd; with it, the crowd costs far more than it earns.
